president.name: Tim d'Aboville & Candela Louzao Carabel
president.bio: Hey! We’re Tim & Candela your JCR Co-Presidents for 2020. We’re second years studying HisPol and Engineering. As Co-Presidents we lead the JCR Committee and act as the key link between students and College. We sit on committees such as CUSU Council and College Council to ensure that your opinions are conveyed to the right people to improve your experience both at uni and at John’s. Alongside our committee we’re working to make John’s the most exciting, most supportive and most enjoyable it can be for you, so if you have any suggestions or issues please feel free to get in touch with us!

vicepresident.name: Anna Stevenson
vicepresident.bio: Hi, I’m Anna, a second year medic and your Vice-President this year! I’m also the Medsoc secretary, SSSK treasurer and a student rep on the Climate Change Committee. As VP, I chair Open meetings, am responsible for the constitution and help out the presidents more generally. My other main job is to organise Freshers week so please get in touch if you have any suggestions or questions about this or anything else.

academic.name: Tom Hasson
academic.bio: Hi, I'm Tom, your Academic Affairs and Careers Officer. I'm a second year Bio-Natsci, as well as LBC for the college boatclub, I sit on the Punt Soc committee, and the Skills Advisory Group for guiding how aspects of courses and colleges should be set up to provide you with necessary skills for careers and life. I'm looking forward to providing a positive academic environment at St John's, as well as career guidance and opportunities. Please feel free to contact me if you have any concerns or requests for anything academic or to do with careers and I'll be happy to help.

access.name: Amy Bottomley
access.bio: Hey everyone! I'm Amy (she/her), your Access Officer for this year. I'm in my third year of English, so I've been here for a while and have tried all sorts of things before settling on what I care about most… Access! As well as being your JCR Access Officer, I'm also on the CSU Class Act committee and act as your college Class Act representative. I've got some really exciting plans for the next year that I can't wait for you all to see. Check out the Access pages for more information on how to get involved and join our John's Access group on Facebook to keep up to date with everything that is going on! I'm always keen to hear any ideas you might have, so feel free to get in touch about anything and everything Access and Class Act related!!

bme.name: Josh Adeyemi
bme.bio: Hi there! I’m Josh, a first year HSPS student, footballer for John's 1st XI and now, your BME Officer for 2020. As BME Officer, I aim to ensure first and foremost that BME members of the college feel included and welcome. I plan to encourage more BME students to apply to John’s through various initiatives in and outside of college. With a particular focus on Black students, who are disproportionately underrepresented at John’s, I want to introduce a John’s BME Open Day and implement a ‘BAMEntor’ scheme which matches prospective applicants of BME heritage with Johnians to enable them to make the most informed application possible. Whilst I look forward to working with fellow JCR members, I also look forward to engaging with fellow students on how John’s can become the most diverse and accessible college at Cambridge.

computing.name: Koji Shukawa
computing.bio: Hey everyone! I’m Koji, your JCR Computing Officer for this year. I’m a first year studying Physical Natural Sciences. As computing officer, I manage the JCR website and help out with any of the technical aspects of the JCR. I also act as a connection between the student body and the IT department to ensure that improvements students feel are important are acted upon. If you have suggestions on how the JCR could use technology to better your experience in college I’d love to know; whether it be something on the website, the Facebook page, or anything in between. Please feel free to email me with any questions!

disabilities.name: Jenny Perratt
disabilities.bio: Hi, I’m Jenny - a first-year geographer and your Disabilities Officer for the year. I’m here to facilitate arrangements needed for students’ disabilities regarding any area of college life, be it pastoral care, academics, or general accessibility. This includes ease of mobility around the college, ensuring accessibility in the new buttery/dining room refurbishments, accommodating learning issues, and mental wellbeing. I’ll also raise awareness within the college for the issues faced by students with disabilities, and liaise with University-level bodies like the Disability Resource Centre and the SU’s Disabled Students Campaign to ensure students are supported outside the college too. Disabilities include mobility issues, health conditions, learning difficulties, and any other condition – and you don’t need to have a diagnosis to seek help from the resources available! Get in touch with me, in person or online, if you have any questions or concerns :)

ents.name: Parth Kotwal
ents.bio: Hey! I'm Parth and I'm your Ents officer for 2020. I'm a second year Engineer and I'm a memberof the St John's rugby team. My job is to organise the college Ents, live music evenings, and other social events within St John's and to ensure that John's remains one of the most fun and social colleges within Cambridge! We usually hold at least three Ents a term in Michaelmas and Lent, along with the rather special June Event as part of our post-exams celebrations in the Easter Term. Make sure to follow the Ents Instagram for the latest updates: @stjohnsents

ethical.name: Emma Warburton
ethical.bio: Hi, I’m Emma, a second year medic and your Ethical and Charitable Affairs Officer for this year. I’m also the Treasurer of John’s MedSoc, as well as a volunteer and representative for several charities. It’s my responsibility to ensure that John’s, as both an institution and community, minimises its environmental impact and promotes the work of charitable organisations. If you’d like to organise an event for charity or have any relevant ideas to discuss, please feel free to get in touch via email.

equalops.name: William Tan
equalops.bio: Hi! I’m Will (he/him), a first-year medic rowing with the college’s Lady Margaret Boat Club and your 2020 Equal Opportunities Officer. I’m excited to continue the work of last year’s Equal Opportunities Officer ensuring St. John’s is an equal, inclusive and friendly community, that is proud to celebrate the diversity of its student body. This could not be achieved without the work of the BAME, LGBT+, International, Women’s, Mental Health and Disabilities officers and the rest of the JCR committee and I’m greatly looking forward to working closely together with them and you to represent and speak for every member of the college family. Ultimately, we would like you to be rest assured that we will work hard to ensure that everyone really feels like St. John’s truly is a home away from home. However, for this to be achieved, I'd like to welcome anyone with any concerns or new and interesting ideas to get in touch with me either by email (wwwt2), or feel free to have a chat if you see me around!

facilities.name: Hugo Lloyd Williams
facilities.bio: Hi, I’m Hugo, a first year History and Politics student and your Facilities Officer for this year! I’m also involved in college mixed netball and college and university rugby. As Facilities Officer, I’m responsible for the Bar, Buttery, Laundry Room and Fitness Centre/Weights Room, and can introduce improvements to these college facilities. So if you have any suggestions or changes you’d like to see, please drop me an email, or use the online form available on the JCR website here and that I will send round towards the end of each term!

internationals.name: Bhanu Balusu
internationals.bio: Hi, I'm Bhanu, a second year engineer, and I'm your international students' officer this year. In this role, I seek to represent and cater to the needs of non-British students. Attending university in a foreign country can bring multiple challenges with it, so feel free to contact me with any questions or concerns that you may have.

mentalhealth.name: Becca Gutteridge
mentalhealth.bio:
Hey, I’m Becca, I’m a second year English student and I’m your ,ental Health Officer! In my spare time I’m VP of John’s Femsoc and Cox for LMBC. Im here to make sure the mental health needs of all students; from wellbeing, right through to mental health problems and long term conditions becoming a disability. Its my aim to make sure all those suffering with mental health issues feel supported, included and have the chance to talk and get the right help -there is lots of support available at John’s if you just ask! 

I will be working with College to improve mental health care and helping you to find out where you can get support. I also think it’s really important to continue the work of the last JCR to improve the mental wellbeing of everyone at John’s. 

“Wellbeing” -being healthy and happy- is so important in such a stress-fuelled environment as Cambridge and helps reduce the risk of/eases management of mental health issues. A big part of my role will also be to improve education and break down stigma surrounding mental health. It really is OK not to be ok, 1/4 of people experience mental health issues and to start feeling better and stop the stigma we need to talk about it!

Come and chat to me any time you see me around college or get in touch via email or Facebook if you need support or have any queries or suggestions!

publicity.name: Paula Espada
publicity.bio: Hello! My name is Paula and I’m a Spanish fresher studying HSPS. I’m also very excited to be your Publicity Officer this year. My role involves managing JCR presence on social media, sending the weekly bulletin and arranging poster displays. Everything to keep you involved and up-to-date! I’m also in charge of the ‘Johnian of the Week’ campaign and promoting all the amazing things Johnians are doing. If there’s anything you’d like to see advertised on social media or the weekly bulletin, feel free to drop me an email. I’ll be happy to hear your suggestions and ideas, too. See you around!

services.name: Zac Bischoff
services.bio: Hi, I’m Zac, this year’s Sports, Services and Societies Officer. I’m a second year Engineer and I play rugby for the Uni 2nds and Redboys and I’ve also represented Johns at volleyball and swimming. I’m the president of the Parson’s Society at Johns and co-captain of the RBBC. My role is to look after the JCR and to support all the college societies and sports teams with anything they might need, so please get in touch if you have any questions, comments or queries for me!

treasurer.name: Martin Limback-Stokin
treasurer.bio: Hi,  I’m Martin, a second year medic and your JCR treasurer for this year.  I’m also involved with college sport and play ice hockey for the University. My role is managing the JCR bank account and ensuring the JCR runs smoothly from a financial standpoint. If any of you have any suggestions or queries about the budget, or more generally about the JCR, feel free to find me around college or drop me an email.

mnb.name: Mark Pepper
mnb.bio: Hi, I’m Mark. I’m a second year studying Maths and I’m part of the Adams society, Cambridge University Hare and Hounds and play college football from time to time. My regular work will involve organising welfare events, running a weekly drop in session and distributing free anonymous sexual health supplies. Please contact me if anything is on your mind, whether you have any worries or issues, an idea for a new welfare event or you just need a chat and a coffee.

fnb.name: Isobel McIntyre
fnb.bio: Hi, I’m Izzy, your female welfare officer this year. I’m a second year studying Engineering and I play netball, frisbee and cox for the college. My role is to support all self-identifying women and non-binary students to keep College as happy and healthy as possible. As well as organising welfare events and providing anonymous sexual health supplies, I’m always available for a chat if you have any welfare concerns and I am able to point you towards someone in the college’s support team if you require further help.

women.name: Eimear Heath
women.bio: Hi, I’m Eimear. I’m a second year studying Biological Natural Sciences. As well as being Treasurer of St John’s Feminist Society, I am actively involved in the Cambridge theatre scene. As Women’s Officer I will advocate for women’s rights within college with the overall purpose of cultivating an environment in St John’s where everyone can feel safe, happy and healthy. I aim to raise awareness of Feminist issues, such as sexual consent, increasing the proportion of women in leadership roles and challenging toxic masculinity. In particular, I am excited to ‘put the fun in Feminism’ through ‘Cake that glass ceiling’ casual chat events and more formal events in collaboration with St John’s Feminist Society. If you have any questions or want a chat, please do not hesitate to get in touch!
